questions.question: Starting with the Brazil release, an administrator wants to use the Basic Auth Restriction page to limit Basic Authentication on the instance without unexpectedly blocking legitimate integrations. What is the recommended sequence?

options.text: Run the tracking period first to identify users relying on Basic Auth, then enable enforcement
Enable enforcement first, then review the blocked requests to build the allowlist
Deactivate Basic Authentication globally with a system property, then re-enable it per user
Assign the admin role to every integration user before enabling enforcement

explanation.correct: The Basic Auth Restriction page limits Basic Authentication access to a defined allowlist. The release notes direct you to run the tracking period first to identify users currently relying on Basic Auth, and then enable enforcement to block Basic Auth requests that don't match the allowlist. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-authentication-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This option reverses the documented order: the release notes say to run the tracking period first and enable enforcement afterward.
The release notes describe an allowlist-based Basic Auth Restriction page with a tracking period, not a global deactivation property.
The release notes do not mention granting the admin role; they describe a tracking period followed by enforcement against an allowlist.

source.excerpt: Run the tracking period first to identify users currently relying on Basic Auth, then enable enforcement to block Basic Auth requests that don't match the allowlist.

questions.question: After upgrading to Brazil, an administrator wants to know what the release adds to warn the team before a SAML SP signing keystore expires and single sign-on starts failing. What does the instance now do?

options.text: It shows home page banners that link to a Security Center customer action
It emails one expiry notice to every user who has the admin role
It renews the expiring keystore by itself and records that in the system log
It suspends SAML single sign-on until the keystore is replaced

explanation.correct: Brazil adds SAML certificate expiry notifications: when SP signing or encryption keystores are nearing or past expiry, administrators get banner alerts on the home page. Separate banners appear for signing and for encryption certificates, and each one links to a dedicated customer action in Security Center so the admin can act before SSO is disrupted. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-authentication-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The new Brazil alerting is home page banner alerts (one for signing, one for encryption certificates). The release notes only say the existing SAML certificate expiry notification now triggers earlier with more keystore detail; they do not describe a single notice emailed to every admin user.
The feature only alerts administrators so they can manage certificates proactively; the release notes do not describe the instance renewing keystores on its own.
The notifications exist so administrators can act before SSO is disrupted and to reduce authentication failures; nothing in the release notes says SSO is suspended.

source.excerpt: The instance displays two separate banners — one for signing certificates and one for encryption certificates — each linking to a dedicated customer action in Security Center.

questions.question: According to the Brazil release notes for Clone Admin Console, which role is required to request, cancel, or schedule clones?

options.text: clone_admin
clone_manager
instance_clone_user
oauth_admin

explanation.correct: The Brazil additional requirements for Clone Admin Console state that the clone_admin role is required to request, cancel, or schedule clones. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-cloneadminconsole-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes name clone_admin, not clone_manager, as the role required to request, cancel, or schedule clones.
The release notes name clone_admin, not instance_clone_user, as the required role.
The release notes name oauth_admin only for the target instance during initial OAuth setup; clone_admin is the role required to request, cancel, or schedule clones.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Clone Admin Console

source.excerpt: The clone_admin role is required to request, cancel, or schedule clones.

questions.question: An administrator is setting up OAuth 2.0 authentication for clone targets in Clone Admin Console. According to the Brazil release notes, when is the oauth_admin role required on the target instance?

options.text: Only during the initial OAuth setup
For every clone request submitted to that target
Whenever a clone is canceled or rescheduled
It is never required; only clone_admin is needed on the target

explanation.correct: The release notes state that the oauth_admin role is required on the target instance during initial OAuth setup only. After the one-time target instance registration, tokens are generated automatically for each clone request, so local admin credentials are not needed on every request. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-cloneadminconsole-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes say oauth_admin is needed on the target during initial OAuth setup only; one-time registration enables automatic token generation for each clone request.
The release notes tie the oauth_admin requirement to initial OAuth setup only, not to canceling or rescheduling clones.
The release notes explicitly state that the oauth_admin role is required on the target instance during initial OAuth setup.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Clone Admin Console

source.excerpt: The oauth_admin role is required on the target instance during initial OAuth setup only.

questions.question: In Clone Admin Console, the Clone Home menu item has been renamed. What is its new name?

options.text: Clone Activity
Clone Overview
Clone Dashboard
Clone Requests

explanation.correct: The release notes state that the Clone Home menu item has been renamed to Clone Activity to better describe the page's purpose and improve navigation clarity. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-cloneadminconsole-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes name Clone Activity, not Clone Overview, as the new name of Clone Home.
The release notes name Clone Activity, not Clone Dashboard, as the new name of Clone Home.
The release notes name Clone Activity, not Clone Requests, as the new name of Clone Home.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Clone Admin Console

source.excerpt: The Clone Home menu item has been renamed to Clone Activity to be more descriptive of the page's purpose and improve navigation clarity.

questions.question: Starting with the Australia release, which role can be granted so administrators can perform basic Data Management tasks without the full admin role?

options.text: data_mgmt_tools_admin
archive_admin
data_policy_admin
table_cleanup_admin

explanation.correct: The release notes describe a granular admin role for Data Management: administrators can perform basic Data Management tasks when granted the data_mgmt_tools_admin role instead of the full admin role. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-datamanagement-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes name data_mgmt_tools_admin, not archive_admin, as the granular Data Management role.
The release notes name data_mgmt_tools_admin, not data_policy_admin, as the granular Data Management role.
The release notes name data_mgmt_tools_admin, not table_cleanup_admin, as the granular Data Management role.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Data Management

source.excerpt: Enable administrators to perform basic Data Management tasks by granting the data_mgmt_tools_admin role instead of the full admin role.

questions.question: In the Australia release, a new Read Only Option was added to the dictionary tables (sys_dictionary and sys_dictionary_override). Which two statements about the documented options are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: With Strict Read Only, the field can't be changed in the UI or by client scripts such as g_form.setValue()
With Display Read Only, the field appears read-only but can still be updated through APIs
With Display Read Only, the field can't be updated by any API
The existing read_only field remains fully editable in the UI
With Strict Read Only, client scripts can still override the read-only setting

explanation.correct: The release notes explain that with Display Read Only the field appears read-only but can still be updated through APIs, and with Strict Read Only the field can't be changed in the UI or by client scripts such as g_form.setValue(). The existing read_only field is now locked and cannot be edited in the UI. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-tablebuilder-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This option reverses the documented behavior: a Display Read Only field can still be updated through APIs.
The release notes state that the existing read_only field is now locked and cannot be edited in the UI.
This option reverses the documented behavior: Strict Read Only fields can't be changed by client scripts such as g_form.setValue().

references: Brazil delta release notes - Table Builder

source.excerpt: With Display Read Only , the field appears read-only but can still be updated through APIs. With Strict Read Only , the field can't be changed in the UI or by client scripts such as [ g_form.setValue() ].

questions.question: Starting with the Australia release, where can an administrator access the ATF troubleshooting agent to troubleshoot failed tests during an upgrade of a non-production instance?

options.text: From the Conduct post-testing step in the post-upgrade activities
From the Pre-upgrade checklist in the Upgrade Console
From the Test Suite Results list in Studio
From the Clone Activity page in Clone Admin Console

explanation.correct: The release notes state that you can troubleshoot failed tests by accessing the ATF troubleshooting agent from the Conduct post-testing step in the post-upgrade activities of a non-production instance. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-upgradeconsole-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes place the ATF troubleshooting agent in the Conduct post-testing step of the post-upgrade activities, not in a pre-upgrade step.
The release notes describe access from the Conduct post-testing step of the Upgrade Console post-upgrade activities, not from Studio.
The release notes describe access from the Upgrade Console post-upgrade activities, not from Clone Admin Console.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Upgrade Console

source.excerpt: You can now troubleshoot failed tests by accessing the ATF troubleshooting agent from the Conduct post-testing step in the post-upgrade activities of a non-production instance.

questions.question: Starting with the Australia release, what is a key benefit of using a declarative action to apply a UI interaction in Configurable Workspace?

options.text: You can extend a page without taking ownership of it
The UI interaction is automatically applied to every workspace on the instance
Client scripts are no longer evaluated on that page
The page is automatically converted to a Core UI form

explanation.correct: The release notes explain that a UI interaction combines logic, script, and configurable UI and can be applied from any page event or declarative action. When you use a declarative action to apply a UI interaction, you can extend a page without taking ownership. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-configurableworkspace-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes describe applying a UI interaction from a page event or declarative action, not automatic application to every workspace.
The release notes do not say client scripts stop being evaluated; the documented benefit is extending a page without taking ownership.
The release notes do not describe any conversion to Core UI; the documented benefit is extending a page without taking ownership.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Configurable Workspace

source.excerpt: When you use a declarative action to apply a UI interaction, you can extend a page without taking ownership.

questions.question: An Employee Center administrator must make the title of the Topic Header widget fit the organization's heading structure so screen reader and keyboard users can navigate pages clearly. Which capability supports this?

options.text: Setting the widget's heading level, H1 to H6, in its instance options
Turning on automatic translation of widgets into the browser language
Applying a high-contrast theme to every portal page for all users
Hiding the widget title so that screen readers skip over the heading

explanation.correct: The Australia and Brazil releases let administrators configure widget heading levels (H1 to H6) to meet organizational standards and support assistive technologies. In Employee Center the admin opens the widget's instance options (for example on the Topic Header widget) and picks the title heading level, giving pages a clear heading hierarchy for screen reader and keyboard users. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-employeecenter-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Employee Center accessibility enhancement in the release notes is configurable widget heading levels; it does not translate widgets, and translation would not fix the heading structure.
A site-wide high-contrast theme is not the capability described; the release notes describe per-widget heading levels from H1 to H6 to build a clear heading hierarchy.
Removing the heading works against the goal: the docs say clear heading hierarchies are what improve navigation for screen reader and keyboard users.

source.excerpt: Improve accessibility by allowing admins to configure widget heading levels (H1–H6) to meet organizational standards and support technologies.

questions.question: An administrator setting up a new Brazil instance wants unregistered users to request accounts and looks for the User Registration Request plugin (com.snc.user_registration). What should the administrator expect?

options.text: It is hidden and not activated on new instances, yet still supported
It is removed from every instance as part of the Brazil upgrade
It is activated by default so the welcome screen shows the request form
It is replaced by a Store app that must be installed before upgrading

explanation.correct: Starting with Brazil, the User Registration Request plugin is being prepared for future deprecation. It is hidden and no longer activated on new instances, but it continues to be supported. The user self-registration docs add that the External User Self-Registration plugin provides the latest experience for this functionality. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-identity-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The plugin is only being prepared for future deprecation; the docs state it will continue to be supported, so it is not removed during the upgrade.
The opposite is true: from Brazil the plugin is hidden and no longer activated on new instances, so the request form is not there by default.
The docs point to the External User Self-Registration plugin for the latest experience, but the old plugin stays supported and nothing must be installed before upgrading.

source.excerpt: Starting with the Brazil release, User Registration Request plugin (com.snc.user_registration) is being prepared for future deprecation. It will be hidden and no longer activated on new instances but will continue to be supported.

questions.question: After the Brazil upgrade, a service desk lead tries to set the Conditional Script Writer group as the assignment group on an incident and cannot select it. What explains this?

options.text: The group is permission-only and is blocked as an assignment group
The upgrade deleted the group and replaced it with a single role
The group now accepts only members who hold the admin role
Auto-assignment must be turned off before the group can be selected

explanation.correct: In Brazil, the Conditional Script Writer group used by the Scripting Governance Tool can no longer be selected as the assignment group on any task-based record or incident through the UI with the base system configuration. The group exists to grant scripting permissions, so it is kept out of operational assignment. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-identity-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The group still exists in Brazil: the Scripting Governance Tool docs say it grants scripting permissions to its members via the snc_required_script_writer_permission role.
Membership is not tied to admin; auto-assignment adds internal users with one functional role, and the group grants snc_required_script_writer_permission.
Auto-assignment controls who becomes a member of the group; the assignment-group restriction applies in the base system configuration regardless of that setting.

source.excerpt: Prevent the Conditional Script Writer group from being selected as the assignment group on task-based records, so the permission-only group is no longer used for operational assignment target.

questions.question: Which legacy user interfaces are deprecated starting with the Australia release, with the Next Experience recommended instead?

options.text: UI11 and UI15
UI16 and Service Portal
Core UI and Workspace
Employee Center and Service Portal

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes name UI11 and UI15, not UI16 and Service Portal, as the deprecated legacy interfaces.
The release notes name UI11 and UI15, not Core UI and Workspace, as the deprecated legacy interfaces.
The release notes name UI11 and UI15, not Employee Center and Service Portal, as the deprecated legacy interfaces.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Next Experience

source.excerpt: Starting with the Australia release, the legacy user interfaces commonly referred to as UI11 and UI15 are deprecated.

questions.question: On a Brazil instance, an administrator wants to add an application menu with a Dashboard module and a List module without leaving the Next Experience UI to edit UI16 platform records. What should the administrator use?

options.text: Next Experience All Menu Editing from the All menu
UI Builder, creating a separate page for each module
A background script that inserts the module records
The classic UI16 application menu and module forms

explanation.correct: Next Experience All Menu Editing lets admins create and edit application menus and modules directly from the Next Experience UI. It supports Record, List, Dashboard and Custom page modules from a centralized, platform-native interface, so there is no need to navigate to UI16 platform records. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-nextexperience-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: UI Builder is not needed here; the release notes say menus and modules are created and edited directly from the Next Experience UI with All Menu Editing.
Scripting the records is unnecessary and error-prone; All Menu Editing offers inline configuration of menus and modules with real-time feedback.
The admin wants to avoid UI16 records, and All Menu Editing exists precisely so admins no longer have to navigate to UI16 platform records.

source.excerpt: Create and edit application menus and modules directly from the Next Experience UI. Admins can configure Record, List, Dashboard, and Custom page modules from a centralized, platform-native interface.

questions.question: Starting with the Brazil release, where can an administrator view the original email associated with a bounced email address?

options.text: From the Bounce Email Address Logs record
Only in the outbound mail server logs outside the instance
From the Email Digest record of the recipient
From the Notification Agent conversation history

explanation.correct: The release notes state that the original email associated with a bounced email address can now be viewed from the Bounce Email Address Logs record. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-notifications-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes say the original email can be viewed from the Bounce Email Address Logs record in the instance.
The release notes name the Bounce Email Address Logs record, not an email digest record.
The release notes name the Bounce Email Address Logs record, not the Notification Agent.

source.excerpt: The original email associated with a bounced email address can now be viewed from the Bounce Email Address Logs record.

questions.question: An administrator enables identifier-first login (IFL) on a Service Portal in Brazil. When a user reaches the portal login page, what determines the authentication path they follow?

options.text: The username or email entered, checked against IFL policies
The browser language and time zone reported by the device
The identity provider selected in the portal's login widget
The highest-privilege role currently held by the user

explanation.correct: With IFL in Service Portal, the login page first shows a username/email field. The authentication path is determined by the username or email entered and is evaluated against the IFL policies configured on the instance, and IFL takes precedence over other login options on the portal. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-serviceportal-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The docs say the path depends on the username or email entered and the configured IFL policies; browser language and time zone are not part of it.
IFL takes precedence over any identity provider or local login options configured for the portal, and admins clear those conflicting options when enabling it.
Roles are not what routes the login; the identifier the user types is evaluated against IFL policies to choose the authentication path.

source.excerpt: Use an identifier-first login (IFL) authentication method in Service Portal where the authentication path is determined by the username or email entered, and evaluated against configured IFL policies.

questions.question: Starting with the Brazil release, an administrator wants to share a Platform Analytics dashboard with all authenticated users without managing individual user, group, or role assignments. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Share it to the dashboard_user role that ships with the base system
Publish its reports so that anyone with the link can view them
Create a group containing every user and then share the dashboard to it
Add each user to the dashboard's sharing list one at a time

explanation.correct: In Brazil, an administrator can share a Platform Analytics dashboard with all authenticated users by assigning it to the dashboard_user role, which ships with the base system. Any user holding at least one role then gets read access, which replaces managing individual user, group, or role assignments for organization-wide dashboards. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-platformanalyticsexperience-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes state it is no longer possible to publish a report; the Read-only link option replaces it and does not share a dashboard organization-wide.
A catch-all group is exactly the kind of group assignment the dashboard_user role approach replaces, and it must be maintained as users join.
Sharing user by user is the individual assignment work the administrator wants to avoid; the dashboard_user role gives every authenticated user read access.

source.excerpt: Administrators can share a Platform Analytics dashboard with all authenticated users by assigning it to the dashboard_user role, which ships with the base system.

questions.question: Starting with the Brazil release, read-only users can use Explore mode on inline dashboards or in the Visualization Designer. Which two statements describe Explore mode? (Choose two.)

options.text: The Save action is not available while Explore mode is active
Users can temporarily reconfigure a visualization in-session without saving changes
Changes are saved as a personal copy of the dashboard
Users must be granted edit access to the dashboard first
Changes are automatically shared with the dashboard owner

explanation.correct: The release notes state that read-only users can temporarily reconfigure a visualization in-session without saving changes. When Explore mode is active, an informational alert indicates that changes aren't persisted and the Save action is not available, so consumers can explore data without edit access. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-platformanalyticsexperience-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes say changes aren't persisted in Explore mode; they do not describe saving a personal copy.
This option reverses the documented behavior: Explore mode lets consumers explore data without requiring edit access.
The release notes say changes aren't persisted; they do not describe sharing changes with the owner.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Platform Analytics experience

source.excerpt: Read-only users can temporarily reconfigure a visualization in-session — on inline dashboards or in the Visualization Designer — without saving changes.

questions.question: Starting with the Australia release, what happens to public Core UI reports on upgrade, and where can report administrators find them?

options.text: They are unpublished; administrators can find them in the Reports Public [sys_report_public] table
They are deleted; administrators must recreate them from backups
They remain public and are copied to the Analytics Hub
They are converted to scheduled exports in the sys_report table

Report administrators can find the unpublished reports on the Reports Public [sys_report_public] table and make them available through the Sharing UI in the Report Designer. wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes say the reports are unpublished, not deleted, and can be found in the Reports Public table.
This option contradicts the release notes: public Core UI reports are unpublished, and the Analytics Hub isn't available after upgrading.
The release notes say the reports are unpublished and listed in the Reports Public [sys_report_public] table, not converted to scheduled exports.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Platform Analytics experience

source.excerpt: On upgrade, all public Core UI reports are unpublished to enhance security control. Report administrators can find the unpublished reports on the Reports Public [sys_report_public] table.

glide.ui.html.editor.textpatterns
glide.choice.empty_label
glide.ui.list.show_none

The release notes name glide.ui.choice.display_none, not glide.choice.empty_label, for this setting.
The release notes name glide.ui.choice.display_none, not glide.ui.list.show_none, for this setting.

questions.question: Starting with the Brazil release, a user has only a catalog-related role and no request management role. What changes for this user regarding the catalog team's ACL records on tables such as Request [sc_request] and Requested Item [sc_req_item]?

options.text: The user can no longer use those ACL records to access request management tables or features
The user automatically receives a request management role during upgrade
Those ACL records now have an empty required roles list
The catalog admin role now grants full access to all request management tables

explanation.correct: The release notes state that ACL records on request management tables and fields no longer grant access based on the catalog role or catalog admin role. Users with only a catalog-related role and no request management role can no longer use these ACL records to access request management tables or features, although another ACL record on the same table might still grant access through a different role. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-servicecatalog-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes do not describe any automatic role assignment during upgrade.
The release notes state that each ACL record retains at least one request management role, so the list is never empty.
This option reverses the documented behavior: these ACL records no longer grant access based on the catalog admin role.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Service Catalog

source.excerpt: Users who have only a catalog-related role and no request management role can no longer use these ACL records to access request management tables or features.
